mainTopic: Marrying a nursing mother, the three-month wait before remarrying, and rules for deciding הלכה from a סתם משנה
overview: The amud opens by explaining why a man may not marry a מינקת חברו: if she becomes pregnant, her milk may dry up and the baby could die. The new husband won't pay for other food, and אביי says she is too embarrassed to sue the יורשים in בית דין. Next, the גמרא explains that the משנה's phrase 'אחת בתולות ואחת בעולות' is one general rule: every woman must wait three months. In a short story, רבי אסי tells רבי אלעזר that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי, who allows betrothal during the wait. A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about women who clearly cannot be pregnant. רבי יוחנן is then reported to have taken back his ruling because of the teaching of the sages in the vineyard of יבנה. Someone asks how רבי יוחנן could rule against a סתם משנה, and רבי אבהו answers with a rule: a סתם followed by a מחלוקת is not binding, while a מחלוקת followed by a סתם is. Finally, רבי נחום asks רבי אבהו how to rule when a משנה and a ברייתא conflict, and the last answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The danger: pregnancy may dry up her milk
steps.stepSummary: The reason a man may not marry a woman nursing another man's baby: she may become pregnant, lose her milk, and the baby may die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps she will become pregnant, her milk will dry up, and she will cause the baby's death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind the rule that a man may not marry a מינקת חברו. The fear is that a new pregnancy will stop her milk and the nursing baby will die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule protects the nursing baby, not the marriage. Pregnancy can stop a woman's milk, so a new marriage could put the baby's life at risk. Every challenge that follows tests this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: her milk becomes spoiled or dries up
she kills him (causes the baby's death)

phrases.english: Perhaps she will become pregnant and her milk will dry up,
and she will kill him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the nursing baby from her earlier husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אִיעַבַּרָה וּמִעֲכַר חַלְבַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a discussion from before this section, giving the reason for the ban on marrying a מינקת חברו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is that pregnancy will dry up her milk and endanger the nursing baby.

steps.title: Then the same danger exists with his own baby
steps.stepSummary: If pregnancy dries up the milk, the same danger should apply when a woman nursing her husband's own baby becomes pregnant again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same should apply to his own child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave. A husband's own wife can also become pregnant while nursing his baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody forbids a married couple to live together while she is nursing their baby. If the danger were only about the milk drying up, that case should also be a problem. So the reason seems incomplete.

phrases.english: If so, his own as well!
phrases.notes: He means the case where she is nursing the husband's own baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, דִּידֵיהּ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that pregnancy endangers the nursing baby
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same danger exists with the husband's own baby, yet that case is permitted.

steps.title: For his own child, she will feed him eggs
steps.stepSummary: With the husband's own child, the parents will feed the baby substitute food such as eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: For his own child, she will feed him with eggs and milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a father takes care of his own baby. If the milk stops, the baby will be fed other food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger is not simply that the milk stops. The danger is that no one will provide a replacement. A father will pay for substitute food for his own child, so his own baby is not at risk.

keyTerms.meaning: she feeds (soft food, by mashing it)

phrases.english: His own, she feeds him with eggs and milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּידֵיהּ — מְמַסְמְסָא לֵיהּ בְּבֵיצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The danger should be the same for any nursing baby.
steps.terutzMaskana: For his own baby there is a substitute food, so there is no danger.

steps.title: She can feed her own baby eggs and milk too
steps.stepSummary: The baby from her earlier husband is still her own child, so she should also feed him eggs and milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her own child too, she will feed him eggs and milk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Even if the baby is not the new husband's, the mother will surely feed her own child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 relied on a parent's care. The mother is also a parent and loves her baby. So the 'substitute food' answer should work in this case as well.

phrases.english: Her own as well,
phrases.notes: He means the baby from her earlier husband is still her own child.

phrases.english: she will feed him with eggs and milk!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּידַהּ נָמֵי, מְמַסְמְסָא לֵיהּ בְּבֵצִים וְחָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between his child and another man's child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The baby is still the mother's child, so she will provide substitute food.

steps.title: The new husband won't pay for it
steps.stepSummary: The new husband will not give her money to feed a child who is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: The husband won't give it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the mother may want to feed the baby, but she depends on her new husband's money. He will not pay for another man's child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is money, not love. The mother lacks the means on her own, and the new husband has no reason to pay. So the baby from the earlier marriage is at risk.

phrases.english: The husband does not give to her.
phrases.notes: He means the new husband won't give her money to buy food for the baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא יָהֵב לַהּ בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother will surely provide substitute food.
steps.terutzMaskana: She cannot afford it, because the new husband will not pay.

steps.title: She could claim support from the heirs
steps.stepSummary: Why can't she sue the first husband's heirs for the baby's support?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her sue the heirs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. The first husband's estate should pay for his baby, so she can go to the יורשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money is the only problem, there is a legal fix. The baby's support can be claimed from the father's estate, so the danger should disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: let her sue them / claim from them

phrases.english: Let her sue the heirs!
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the usual printed גמרא, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean she should take the heirs to court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִתְבְּעִינְהוּ לְיוֹרְשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that she has no money to feed the baby
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She has a legal way to get money from the first husband's heirs.

steps.title: אביי: she is too embarrassed to go to court
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a woman is embarrassed to go to בית דין, so in practice the baby goes without food.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A woman is embarrassed to come to court, and so she kills her son.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the last challenge. In real life, a woman will avoid going to בית דין, so the baby will not get proper food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a legal right does not mean she will use it. Embarrassment keeps her from suing, and the baby suffers. That is why the rabbis forbade marrying a מינקת חברו.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on marrying a מינקת חברו protects the nursing baby. Pregnancy may stop the milk, the new husband won't pay for food, and the mother is too embarrassed to sue the יורשים.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A woman is embarrassed to come to court,
and she kills her son.
phrases.notes: She doesn't kill him on purpose. By not going to court, she ends up causing his death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִשָּׁה בּוֹשָׁה לָבֹא לְבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 and closes this discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She can always claim support from the heirs.
steps.terutzMaskana: Embarrassment stops her from going to court, so the danger remains.

steps.title: The משנה's words seem to repeat themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה 'אחת בתולות ואחת בעולות' and asks how בתולות differ from ארוסות, and how בעולות differ from נשואות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Both virgins and non-virgins.' Who are the virgins, and who are the betrothed? Who are the non-virgins, and who are the married?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the משנה about the three-month wait and asks why the משנה seems to list the same women twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothed woman is usually a virgin, and a married woman is a non-virgin. If the משנה also lists ארוסות and נשואות, the words בתולות and בעולות seem to add nothing. The גמרא wants to know what each term covers.

phrases.english: Both virgins and non-virgins.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about women who must wait three months before remarrying.

phrases.aramaic: הֵי נִיהוּ בְּתוּלוֹת וְהֵי נִיהוּ אֲרוּסוֹת?
phrases.english: Which are virgins and which are betrothed?

phrases.aramaic: הֵי נִיהוּ בְּעוּלוֹת וְהֵי נִיהוּ נְשׂוּאוֹת?
phrases.english: Which are non-virgins and which are married?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי נִיהוּ בְּתוּלוֹת וְהֵי נִיהוּ אֲרוּסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the terms בתולות and בעולות add beyond ארוסות and נשואות.

steps.title: It is one general rule, not separate groups
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that the משנה gives one rule: virgins and non-virgins, widowed or divorced, from betrothal or from marriage, all must wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said, this is what it means: both virgins and non-virgins who were widowed or divorced, whether from betrothal or from marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the question. The משנה is not listing separate groups of women. It is saying that the wait applies to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the words do not repeat. 'Widowed or divorced' describes how the earlier relationship ended, 'from betrothal or from marriage' describes what stage it had reached, and 'virgins or non-virgins' describes the woman. Together they mean the rule has no exceptions.
steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'אחת בתולות ואחת בעולות' is one broad rule. The three-month wait applies to every woman, however her earlier marriage or betrothal ended.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said, this is what it is saying:
both virgins and non-virgins
who were widowed or divorced,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין.
phrases.english: whether from betrothal or from marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה states one general rule that covers all women, not separate groups.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks what was taught in the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר missed the study hall one day. He met רבי אסי and asked what the rabbis had said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר did not go to the study hall. He found רבי אסי and asked him: What did the rabbis say in the study hall?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a short story. This line sets up the ruling that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows how a ruling was passed on to a scholar who was absent. The question itself teaches nothing new. Its purpose is to introduce רבי יוחנן's ruling.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא עָל לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar did not enter the study hall.
He found Rabbi Asi,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא?
phrases.english: he said to him: What did the Sages say in the study hall?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא עָל לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that leads to a ruling on the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ruling was taught in the study hall that day.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reports that רבי יוחנן ruled the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who allows betrothal within the three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers רבי אלעזר with a ruling from רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי holds that women may become betrothed before the three months are over, except for a widow. Betrothal alone does not lead to living together, so the reason for the wait does not apply. רבי יוחנן decides the הלכה this way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical ruling: within the three-month wait, betrothal is allowed even though marriage is not.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him, this is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן ruled that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר infers that a lone opinion disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks: since רבי יוחנן had to state the הלכה, does that mean a single opinion argues on this?
steps.simpleTranslation: From this, does it follow that an individual opinion disagrees with him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר hears רבי יוחנן's ruling and asks whether it means some lone opinion disagrees. This question sets up רבי אסי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling of 'the הלכה follows X' is normally said when there is a real argument. So רבי אלעזר reasons that if רבי יוחנן needed to state it, there must be a single opinion on the other side. He wants to know who that is.

keyTerms.meaning: From the implication of; it follows that

phrases.english: Does it follow that an individual disagrees with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דִּיחִידָאָה פְּלִיג עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ruling רבי אסי just reported.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a lone opinion that disagrees, which made רבי יוחנן's ruling necessary?

steps.title: רבי אסי confirms the dispute with a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says yes and quotes a ברייתא. In it, רבי מאיר requires even women who clearly cannot be pregnant to wait three months, and רבי יהודה lets them marry right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, and so it is taught: a woman who kept running off to her father's house, or had anger in her husband's house, or whose husband was in prison, or was old or sick, or she herself was sick, or she miscarried after her husband died, or she was barren, old, a minor, an אילונית, or could not give birth for any reason, still must wait three months. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה allows her to be betrothed and to marry immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי confirms there is a dispute and brings a ברייתא to show it. He lists many women who certainly are not pregnant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-month wait exists to make clear who the father of a baby is. The ברייתא lists women for whom that worry seems not to apply, either because she was not living with her husband or because she cannot be pregnant at all. רבי מאיר still requires the wait, while רבי יהודה says she may marry at once. So there really is an argument on this topic.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose body never developed the ability to bear children

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the three-month wait is a fixed rule for רבי מאיר, even when its reason does not apply in a given case. רבי יהודה disagrees.

phrases.english: Yes, and so it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיְתָה רְדוּפָה לֵילֵךְ לְבֵית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: A woman who was always rushing off to her father's house,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ כַּעַס בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ,
phrases.english: or she had anger in her husband's house,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעְלָהּ חָבוּשׁ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: or her husband was locked up in prison,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעְלָהּ זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה,
phrases.english: or her husband was old or sick,
or she herself was sick,
or she miscarried after her husband's death,
or she was barren, or old,
or a minor, or an aylonit,
or she is unable to give birth —
she must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר לֵיאָרֵס וְלִינָּשֵׂא מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda permits her to be betrothed and to marry immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's question by bringing a ברייתא that shows an argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, there is a dispute: רבי מאיר requires the wait even when pregnancy is impossible, and רבי יהודה permits immediate marriage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing women who cannot be pregnant

steps.title: רבי יוחנן changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that רבי יוחנן took back his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new voice, רבי חייא בר אבא, reports that רבי יוחנן changed his mind about the ruling רבי אסי quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי, who allows betrothal within the three months. Now we hear he took that ruling back. This changes the picture, and the next step explains why he retracted.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted; he changed his mind

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יוחנן (the אמורא whose ruling is discussed) with רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה in the next step. They are different people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yochanan retracted.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן took back his ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: חָזַר בּוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 11 and reports that he withdrew it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן no longer holds that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The vineyard ברייתא caused the retraction
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that if רבי יוחנן retracted, it was because of the ברייתא from the sages in the vineyard of יבנה, who said all these women must wait three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If he retracted, he retracted because of the ברייתא of the vineyard. As it is taught: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה said, 'I heard from the sages in the vineyard in יבנה: all of them must wait three months.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains what made רבי יוחנן change his mind. He points to a ברייתא in which the great sages of יבנה ruled that all these women must wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'vineyard in יבנה' was the meeting place of the main sages of that generation. They ruled that 'all of them', meaning even the women listed in the earlier ברייתא, must wait three months. A ruling from that group is strong enough to make רבי יוחנן drop his earlier position.

keyTerms.meaning: The teaching of the vineyard; the ברייתא from the sages of יבנה
He retracted (Aramaic form of חזר בו)
The vineyard in יבנה, where the sages gathered to learn

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If he retracted —
it was because of the teaching of the vineyard that he retracted.
As it is taught: Rabbi Yishmael said,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה,
phrases.english: the son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka:
I heard from the mouth of the sages in the vineyard in Yavneh:
All of them must wait three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source behind the retraction reported in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's retraction from ruling like רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the sages in the vineyard of יבנה, reported by רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's own rule about an unattributed משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה tells רבי זריקא to raise a contradiction before רבי אבהו. רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and our משנה says without a name that all women must wait three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זריקא: When you come before רבי אבהו, raise this contradiction: Did רבי יוחנן really say the הלכה follows רבי יוסי? But רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and we learned: 'All women may not marry or be betrothed until three months have passed, both virgins and non-virgins!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge against the report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי. It uses רבי יוחנן's own general rule against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a known principle: when a משנה states a law without naming who said it, that is the הלכה. Our משנה says without any name that all women must wait three months. So how could רבי יוחנן rule like רבי יוסי, who allows betrothal within that time?

keyTerms.meaning: Raise a contradiction to him; literally 'throw at him'
An unattributed משנה, with no name of a sage

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'הלכה כסתם משנה' is one of רבי יוחנן's main principles for deciding הלכה. That is why this contradiction carries real weight.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זְרִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zerika:
When you go in before Rabbi Abbahu,

phrases.aramaic: רְמִי לֵיהּ: מִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: raise this contradiction to him: Did Rabbi Yochanan really say
the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כִּסְתַם מִשְׁנָה.
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan said: the halacha follows an unattributed Mishnah.

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים לֹא יִנָּשְׂאוּ וְלֹא יִתְאָרְסוּ
phrases.english: And we learned: All women may not marry and may not be betrothed
until they have waited three months,
both virgins and non-virgins!

steps.triggerLanguage: רְמִי לֵיהּ: מִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling attributed to רבי יוחנן in step 11 by using his own principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן ruled the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן holds הלכה כסתם משנה. The unattributed משנה requires all women to wait three months, so he should not rule like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: An unnamed ruling followed by a dispute is not binding
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the contradiction is weak. Our משנה is a סתם that is later followed by a מחלוקת, so the הלכה does not have to follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Whoever raised this contradiction for you didn't think it through. This is an unnamed ruling that is later followed by a dispute, and in that case the הלכה is not like the unnamed ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the contradiction רבי זריקא brought him. He says the rule 'follow the סתם משנה' does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction assumed that רבי יוחנן must follow every סתם משנה. רבי אבהו explains that the order matters. When a סתם comes first and a מחלוקת comes after it, the סתם is not the final word, so רבי יוחנן was free to rule against it.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'not concerned for his flour'; he didn't put careful thought into it
an unnamed ruling, stated with no rabbi's name attached

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אבהו is throwing out the rule 'the הלכה follows a סתם משנה.' He is only saying it does not work when the סתם comes first and a dispute comes after.

phrases.english: He said to him: the one who raised this contradiction for you
is not concerned for his flour.
phrases.notes: It's an expression: he didn't take care with his own 'flour,' meaning he didn't think the question through.

phrases.english: It is an unnamed ruling followed afterward by a dispute,
phrases.notes: The unnamed ruling is the משנה from step 16, where all the women wait three months.

phrases.english: and the halacha is not like the unnamed ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּרְמָא לָךְ הָא לָא חַשׁ לְקִמְחֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule: the rule about a סתם משנה depends on the order in which the סתם and the dispute appear.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every סתם משנה decides the הלכה, so רבי יוחנן could not have ruled like רבי יוסי against our unnamed משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A סתם that is followed by a מחלוקת does not decide the הלכה, so רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יוסי does not contradict his rule.

steps.title: רב פפא's rule about the order of unnamed rulings and disputes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו backs up his answer with a rule from רב פפא (some say רבי יוחנן). A dispute followed by a סתם means follow the סתם. A סתם followed by a dispute means do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב פפא said, and some say it was רבי יוחנן: If there is a dispute and afterward an unnamed ruling, the הלכה follows the unnamed ruling. If there is an unnamed ruling and afterward a dispute, the הלכה does not follow the unnamed ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what רבי אבהו just said. It is an established rule about which version, the earlier or the later one, counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that whatever comes later counts as the final summary. If the משנה ends with an unnamed ruling, it chose one side. If it ends with a dispute, the question was left open.

keyTerms.meaning: some say; it marks a second opinion on who said the statement
a dispute first, then an unnamed ruling; the הלכה follows the סתם
an unnamed ruling first, then a dispute; the הלכה does not follow the סתם

steps.whatToRemember: The later version wins. A dispute followed by a סתם means follow the סתם. A סתם followed by a dispute means the סתם is not binding.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule of how to decide הלכה from the משנה, and it is used in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: As Rav Pappa said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yochanan:
A dispute, and afterward an unnamed ruling:
the halacha is like the unnamed ruling.
An unnamed ruling, and afterward a dispute:
the halacha is not like the unnamed ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אבהו's answer in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a סתם followed by a מחלוקת does not decide the הלכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule stated by רב פפא, or by רבי יוחנן himself according to the other version.

steps.title: רבי נחום gathers הלכות from רבי אבהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the scene. רבי אבהו used to walk leaning on his attendant רבי נחום, who would learn הלכות from him along the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו would walk leaning on the shoulder of רבי נחום, his attendant, and רבי נחום would gather הלכות from him as they walked.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story that sets up the next move. It introduces the questions רבי נחום is about to ask רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling is given here yet. The story tells us that the questions coming next were real questions asked of רבי אבהו, which gives his answers a firm source.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu would walk along, leaning
on the shoulder of Rabbi Nachum, his attendant,
and he would walk along gathering halachos from him.
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is רבי נחום, who was learning from רבי אבהו as they walked.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתְּמִיךְ וְאָזֵיל רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אַכַּתְפֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי נַחוּם שַׁמָּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that confirms the rule from step 18 through רבי אבהו's own answers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. It sets up רבי נחום's questions to רבי אבהו.

steps.title: רבי נחום asks about the order of unnamed ruling and dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחום asks about both orders. רבי אבהו answers: if the dispute comes first and the סתם after, follow the סתם; if the סתם comes first and the dispute after, do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: If there is a dispute and afterward an unnamed ruling, what is the law? He said: The הלכה is like the unnamed ruling. If there is an unnamed ruling and afterward a dispute, what is the law? He said: The הלכה is not like the unnamed ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחום asks two questions about rulings that are both in the משנה, and רבי אבהו answers each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answers match the rule of רב פפא in step 18 exactly. This shows that רבי אבהו himself held this rule, which explains why he answered the contradiction the way he did.

phrases.english: He asked him:
A dispute and afterward an unnamed ruling, what is the law?
He said to him: The halacha is like the unnamed ruling.
An unnamed ruling and afterward a dispute, what is the law?
He said to him: The halacha is not like the unnamed ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ: מַחְלוֹקֶת וְאַחַר כָּךְ סְתָם מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first questions in the story from step 19; the answers confirm the rule from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to rule when a סתם and a מחלוקת both appear in the משנה, in each of the two orders.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dispute then סתם: follow the סתם. סתם then dispute: do not follow the סתם.

steps.title: Unnamed ruling in a משנה against a dispute in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחום now asks about a משנה against a ברייתא. A סתם in the משנה with a dispute in a ברייתא: follow the סתם. Then he asks about a dispute in the משנה with a סתם in a ברייתא, and the answer begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה has an unnamed ruling and a ברייתא has a dispute, what is the law? He said: The הלכה is like the unnamed ruling. If the משנה has a dispute and a ברייתא has an unnamed ruling, what is the law? He said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחום moves to a new kind of case, where the סתם and the dispute come from different sources: one from a משנה and the other from a ברייתא. The second answer continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה carries more weight than a ברייתא. So a סתם in the משנה holds even if a ברייתא records a dispute about it. The open question is whether a סתם in a ברייתא can settle a dispute recorded in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: an unnamed ruling in the משנה
a teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the question is not about which ruling comes first. It is about which source is stronger, a משנה or a ברייתא.

phrases.english: An unnamed ruling in the Mishnah
and a dispute in a Baraita, what is the law?
He said to him: The halacha is like the unnamed ruling.
A dispute in the Mishnah
and an unnamed ruling in a Baraita, what is the law?
He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי אבהו's answer continues on the next part of the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְתָמָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין וּמַחְלוֹקֶת בְּבָרַיְיתָא, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the questions from step 20 to cases where a משנה is set against a ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to rule when the סתם and the dispute come from different sources, a משנה and a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סתם in the משנה against a dispute in a ברייתא: follow the סתם. The answer for a dispute in the משנה with a סתם in a ברייתא continues on the next part of the daf.
